findings.issue: kana contains the extra syllables きごう, which is the reading of 記号 ('symbol') — the tokenizer's POS label for the ASCII space in the jp — not anything pronounced in the sentence. A learner would read a nonexistent word.
findings.current: でわきごうおさきにしつれいします
findings.suggested: でわおさきにしつれいします

findings.issue: romaji contains the spurious word 'kigou' (reading of the space token's 記号 tag), inherited from the corrupted kana. Not covered by the known punctuation/katakana issue — it is a wrong extra word.

Token 2 has surface " " (a space) with reading きごう. きごう is the name of the tokenizer's symbol POS (記号), not a pronunciation; a whitespace token has no reading. Remove the token or null its reading — it is the root cause of the kana/romaji corruption.
findings.suggested: null (remove the whitespace token or clear its reading)

findings.issue: Generated Japanese contains a stray ASCII space after では. Japanese does not use spaces; standard writing is no space or a comma. The space is what triggered the 記号 tokenizer artifact downstream.
findings.current: では お先に失礼します
findings.suggested: では、お先に失礼します

findings.issue: Sub-tokens 万年 (tokens[0]) and 筆 (tokens[1]) are stranded at the start of the token list, before 父, while the compound 万年筆 sits at position 4. Sequential rendering yields 万年筆父に万年筆をもらった. Elsewhere (sent:gen-339c361f48f0, 水曜/日/水曜日) sub-tokens immediately precede their compound.
findings.current: tokens list opens with 万年(まんねん), 筆(ひつ) before 父
findings.suggested: Move 万年 and 筆 to directly before the 万年筆 token (after を's antecedent 父に), matching the 水曜日 sub-token pattern

findings.issue: expl_pt glosses 私の妹 as 'minha irmã', dropping the 'younger' meaning of 妹 that expl_en correctly gives ('my younger sister'). The 妹/姉 distinction is core vocabulary, and the two explanation languages should be consistent.
findings.current: usa a partícula の para indicar posse ('minha irmã')
findings.suggested: usa a partícula の para indicar posse ('minha irmã mais nova')
